study: Laya step 2: do int8 and bf16 keep Laya's decisions and calibration against fp32 on the CPU?
frozen: before any int8 or bf16 arm is scored on the items; the fp32 reference was scored first

items.note: each task's first rows of its test split, built as the model card's runs built them; the fixture is receptron's reference ticket (no gold)

int8_dyn.what: step 1's copy: ORT dynamic quantization, per-channel int8 weights on the 120 MatMuls with constant weights, a per-call activation scale; the 4 head Gemms stay fp32

bf16_emul.what: all 124 MatMul/Gemm with constant 2-D weights: weights rounded to bf16 (nearest, ties to even), a Cast pair rounding each one's activation input; fp32 accumulate, fp32 out; attention products, norms and embeddings fp32

criteria_text.C0: the scored file is the pre-registered arm (both file hashes)
criteria_text.C1: the same top option as fp32 on at least this share of the 2,400 labelled items, pooled
criteria_text.C2: pooled accuracy no more than 0.5 pt below fp32's
criteria_text.C3: each task's accuracy no more than 1.5 pt below fp32's
criteria_text.C4: pooled ECE at T=1 no more than 0.010 above fp32's
criteria_text.C5: each task's ECE at T=1 no more than 0.020 above fp32's

c1_rule: 0.99, lowered to 1 - (items whose fp32 top-two gap at the shipped temperatures is under 0.048) / 2400 when that is lower, rounded down to 0.5%: never tighter than what the authors' own torch bf16 shift (max |dp| 0.024 on choice questions) could flip on these items
decision: an arm PASSES iff C0-C5 all hold. int8 failing removes int8 from an NPU build of Laya; bf16 failing as well stops the NPU numeric path for Laya at these schemes. Speed is step 3's question.
why_t1: calibration is judged at T=1: the shipped choice:11+ temperature (0.1006) multiplies logit shifts about 10x on Banking77 and MASSIVE, and laya's current package clamps temperatures to [0.5, 5]
reported_not_deciding: |dp| at T=1 and at the shipped temperatures
